correctness.rationale: For Euclidean-motion-invariant line measure, a segment of length s is hit with measure 2s, and a convex polygon is hit with measure equal to its perimeter. The union of line-hit events for the two adjacent sides AB and BC equals the triangle ABC line-hit event up to a null set. Inclusion-exclusion gives joint incidence measure |AB|+|BC|-|AC|. Normalizing by polygon perimeter therefore recovers all consecutive side lengths and two-step diagonals. The cosine law recovers every turning angle; ordered side vectors reconstruct all vertices uniquely up to similarity and reflection. Exact feasibility follows from the strict local triangle inequalities, total exterior turn 2pi and vector closure: strictly monotone edge directions and closure force all intermediate vertices to the same strict side of each supporting edge. Local stability is a smooth inverse away from zero side lengths and 0/pi angles. The attached executable corroborates 1,162 comparisons but finite tests are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The distinctive assertion is reconstruction and exact realizability of all labeled strictly convex polygons using only individual side-hit and adjacent-side pair-hit probabilities for isotropic random lines. Classical Cauchy–Crofton, segment hit measures, inclusion-exclusion and cosine law are not novel. Inspected primary works obtain full scalar chord-length distributions for regular polygons or use richer direction-resolved probing; their stated theorems do not provide this sparse incidence inverse and global closure feasibility equivalence. Priority is qualified by older works that could not be fully inspected.
residual_risks: Older integral-geometry texts or articles may present the same triangle side-event identity explicitly as a polygon inverse theorem; not all historical literature is text searchable.
Full papers by Gates (1982), Nagel (1993) and Edelsbrunner–Skiena (1988) were not available for line-by-line comparison.
A different equivalently formulated sparse edge-and-angle inverse may be described elsewhere; this work has not undergone independent historical-priority review.

value.rationale: The observable is natural in random-line stereology: which of the labeled polygon boundary sides a random line crosses. Rather than compute a single mean or a fixed regular-polygon case, the theorem gives an explicit all-polygon shape inverse and a necessary-and-sufficient global feasibility classification for only 2n local probabilities, including the nontrivial fact that closure and total turning suffice for strict convexity. It identifies a reduced n-observable law for equilateral polygons and proves local stability for nondegenerate shapes. The result is a mathematically motivated complete structural classification, while statistical finite-sample recovery is excluded.
